analyzed_vuln.description: `RecordBatchFileReaderImpl::ReadFooter()` reads the 4-byte footer length using `*reinterpret_cast<const int32_t*>(buffer->data())` (line ~644) without using a safe unaligned load helper. This can produce a corrupted/host-endian-dependent `footer_length` from fuzzed bytes, which is then trusted to locate footer blocks. Later, `ReadMessageFromBlock()` passes attacker-controlled `block.metadata_length` into `ReadMessage()`, where `SafeLoadAs<int32_t>(buffer->data())` dereferences an invalid pointer and crashes. The crash is observed in `ReadMessage`/`SafeLoadAs`, but the root cause is insufficient validation/safe parsing of footer-derived block metadata in `ReadFooter` path.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In `arrow-ipc-file-fuzz`, attacker input is treated as an IPC file. The file must pass basic magic/footer checks enough to reach footer parsing, then provide crafted footer/block values (especially dictionary block metadata_length/offset) so `ReadDictionaries()` -> `ReadMessageFromBlock()` calls `ReadMessage()` with invalid metadata parameters. This leads to a wild read when loading the continuation token from the returned buffer in `SafeLoadAs<int32_t>`. The PoV’s malformed footer/block table with many 0xFF fields satisfies this.
